correctness.rationale: The sufficient direction is a valid geometric-subsequence Borel-Cantelli argument: finite logarithmic moment makes the sampled tail probabilities summable, while bounded upward growth fills gaps and letting the ratio tend to one forces tau_n/n to zero. For sharpness, divergence of the dyadic log-tail sum and independent block activations yield infinitely many active blocks; the constructed process respects unit upward growth, nondecreasing timestamps, and pointwise domination by T, with endpoint ratios tending to 1/2. The harmonic-window bound follows from tau_n/n to zero.
risks: The converse is existential; it does not say every process with an infinite-log dominator has linear spikes.

evidence: Sharp sufficiency/converse pair and direct harmonic-window consequence.
value.rationale: This identifies a sharp structural threshold for a mechanism central to heavy-tailed asynchronous stochastic approximation, admits dominators with no finite positive moment, and gives a matching failure construction. It is a substantive boundary theorem rather than a routine weakening.
risks: Other assumptions of the stochastic-approximation convergence theorems remain necessary.

final_claim: For age-of-information processes with a common stochastic dominator and bounded upward increments, finite E log(1+T) is the sharp universal threshold for almost-sure sublinear age; when it diverges there is a unit-growth dominated process with limsup tau_n/n at least 1/2, and sublinear age implies a vanishing harmonic stale window.
limitations: Universal threshold under common stochastic domination and bounded upward age increments only.
No finite-time rates or all-step-size optimality.
